text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Citizens in the Italian-speaking Swiss canton of Ticino will vote on April 20 on a referendum sponsored by trade unions to cut back late opening hours for shops twice a week.
- The World Trade Organisation in Geneva reported the growth rate of world trade in goods and services fell to below six percent in 1996 from the year before.
- Crossair, a subsidiary of Swissair, expanded considerably in 1996. The number of passengers flying on the airline rose by 73 percent to 3.97 million.
- U.S. group Baxter International is taking over Lugano-based Bieffe Medical for $185 million.
- Though the number of firms in Switzerland's paper and carton industry fell from 27 to 25 in 1996, production rose by 1.8 percent to 1.46 million tons.
- Credit Suisse will be the first Swiss bank to offer banking on the Internet starting April 14.
- Pilatus Fluegzeugwerke AG in Stans took over Geneva-based TSA Transairco SA.
